study_label: Auditory peripersonal space in humans. (a)
title: Auditory peripersonal space in humans.
experiment_label: Experiment 1 — right-side front/back × near/far × sound type
auditory_stimulus: Static free-field wideband white-noise bursts and 1.5-kHz pure tones, level-adjusted to 70 dB at the ear and emitted by a 0.3-W, 8-ohm loudspeaker under sensor/switch control; reusable source waveforms are not supplied.
trajectory_kinematics: Static right-front and right-back sources at 20 or 70 cm from the head, ear level and 45 degrees from the sagittal plane; sound lasts for the tactile contact (brief, under 1 s), so motion speed is not applicable.
trial_sequence: One tactile-only baseline condition plus eight cross-modal blocks (2 sound types x front/back x 20/70 cm). Each 40-trial block used 10 single-left, 10 single-right, 10 bilateral/simultaneous and 10 no-stimulation rows in the same pseudorandom order; the full protocol ran twice.
task_response: After an experimenter attention prompt, participants verbally reported left, right, both, or none after each event, regardless of modality.
jitter_iti_policy: No ITI, inter-trial interval, jitter value, or distribution was recovered after the main-PDF, targeted, fallback, and supplement-route checks.
soa_schedule: Cross-modal sound and touch were simultaneous (nominal 0-ms SOA); there was no varied SOA ladder.
tactile_target: Brief light contact under 1 s with a 1-cm² touch-sensitive sensor on the lateral neck behind the ear, below the mastoid process.
baseline_trial_contract: Tactile-only switch-off baseline with the same manual contact timing: one 40-trial condition x two protocol runs = 80 baseline-block trials (60 tactile-present and 20 no-stimulation).
catch_trial_contract: No-stimulation rows required a 'none' report: 9 conditions x 10 no-stimulation trials x 2 protocol runs = 180, of which 160 were in cross-modal blocks and 20 in tactile-only baseline blocks.
repetition_allocation: Nine condition blocks, each with 10 repetitions of four trial types, repeated in two complete protocol runs: 9 x 40 x 2 = 720 trials per participant (640 cross-modal-block trials and 80 baseline-block trials).
block_order_contract: Nine condition-specific 40-trial blocks per protocol, with condition-block order randomized across sessions and participants; the complete protocol was repeated twice, yielding 18 blocks.

study_label: Extended multisensory space in blind cane users. (a)
title: Extended multisensory space in blind cane users.
experiment_label: Static near/far hand PPS with cane and handle conditions
auditory_stimulus: Stimulus type: Auditory stimuli were 150 ms bursts of white noise. | Source provenance: Sounds were generated by two identical loudspeakers; phono-spectral waves were recorded by computer to verify equal sounds at the origin. | Auditory conditions: Near versus far sound location was crossed with weak target, strong nontarget, and sound-only catch rows; tool state was manipulated in separate cane/handle/training blocks. | Gain envelope: Near and far sounds were equalized to 70 dB at the participant's ear; sounds were also checked for equality at origin. | Renderer or apparatus: Two identical loudspeakers placed near and far from the stimulated hand; XGen software controlled stimulus presentation and response recording.
trajectory_kinematics: Trajectory path: Near sound was close to the stimulated right hand; far sound was on the floor about 125 cm from the hand, corresponding to average cane length and the fixed cane-tip location. | Stimulus duration: Auditory white-noise bursts lasted 150 ms. | Stimulus speed: No looming or moving auditory stimulus was used; near and far sounds were static speaker locations. | Trajectory count: Two static auditory positions/conditions: near the stimulated hand and far on the floor near the cane tip. | Gain envelope: Near and far sounds were equalized to 70 dB at the participant's ear; sounds were also checked for equality at origin. | Renderer or apparatus: Two identical loudspeakers placed near and far from the stimulated hand; XGen software controlled stimulus presentation and response recording.
trial_sequence: Weak tactile targets, strong tactile nontargets and sound-only catches paired with static near/far auditory locations.
task_response: Task sequence rules: Subjects verbally responded only to weak tactile targets, ignored sounds, received 30 familiarization trials before the experiment, and should not respond on strong nontarget or sound-only catch trials.
soa_schedule: Near: source and tactile onset simultaneous. Far: source starts 5 ms before touch, so tactile-minus-source SOA is+5 ms.
tactile_target: Tactile stimulus: Two DS7A Digitimer constant-current stimulators delivered weak target and strong nontarget electrical stimuli through Neuroline electrodes on the upper side of the right index finger; intensities were calibrated to about 90% and 100% perception.
baseline_trial_contract: Baseline strategy: No separate tactile-only baseline is reported; the task estimates PPS effects from near-versus-far sound comparisons across handle/cane/training conditions. | Baseline timing: No tactile-only baseline SOA schedule was used or reported. | Baseline count: No separate tactile-only baseline trials are reported.
catch_trial_contract: 30 sound-only catches plus 60 strong tactile no-go trials;90 no-response rows in total.
repetition_allocation: 30 trials for each of 4 tactile-strength x sound-location cells, plus 30 sound-only catches:150 per described task.
block_order_contract: Cane and handle conditions for all participants; sighted participants additionally tested immediately and one day after cane training.

experiment_label: Computational model fitted to prior data; no new human acquisition
auditory_stimulus: Cited human-task summary describes 3000-ms sounds with a 55–70 dB exponential rise; this computational paper does not generate new empirical acquisition audio.
trajectory_kinematics: 30 cm/s is an explicit model assumption because the empirical speed was not reported. Seven delays map to model spatial inputs; this is not a measured moving-source trajectory.
trial_sequence: The model fits existing behavioral curves and manipulates neural architecture/noise. No new acquired human trial stream.
task_response: Model RT is a tactile-neuron activation threshold crossing at 90% maximum, then linearly rescaled to behavioral data; it is not a participant button timestamp.
jitter_iti_policy: No new human acquisition interval. Model integration/simulation times are not ITI settings.
soa_schedule: Seven delays between 300 and 2700 ms are represented in the model. Human acquisition parameters belong to the cited empirical source, not a new study here.
tactile_target: Model represents a 10 x 5 cm left-hand skin area while describing the prior task as right-hand stimulation. Its 100-ms neural inputs differ from the cited 100-microsecond stimulation; these are model conventions.
baseline_trial_contract: The healthy-control network fitted to an existing average curve is a model baseline, not an extra human control trial.
catch_trial_contract: No new human catch/no-go acquisition. A simulation paper cannot establish catch absence in the original experiment.

title: Using Android Smartphones to Collect Precise Measures of Reaction Times to Multisensory Stimuli.
auditory_stimulus: 3250-ms burst-train files, sampled at 44.1 kHz, spatialized in Max/MSP 6.1.10 with Spat and LISTEN HRTFs.

trial_sequence: 300-ms silence, 3250-ms fixed/looming sound with touch on target rows, then 1000-1400-ms silence.
task_response: Tap the smartphone screen on detecting left-hand vibration; ignore sound and avoid anticipation.
jitter_iti_policy: 300-ms leading silence and a random 1000-1400-ms trailing silence after audio.
tactile_target: 155-Hz, 50-ms maximum-amplitude phone-motor vibration to the left hand holding the device.
baseline_trial_contract: Fixed-far sound control: 144 target trials across six delays, derived from 24 repetitions per condition.
catch_trial_contract: 24 catches per block x 6 = 144, and 432 total minus 288 targets = 144, but prose states 184 catches.
repetition_allocation: Six blocks x 72 = 432 trials, 288 targets; catch prose says 184 while arithmetic gives 144.
block_order_contract: Six experimental blocks with short breaks and a mandatory ten-minute halfway break; duration descriptions disagree.
